Traupman 253

duodecim

numeral, indeclinable, declension

twelve

Latin has no word for a dozen and does not count in dozens: a dozen eggs are duodecim ōva.

Other words

  • duodēnī, duodēnae, duodēna — twelve each, twelve at a time

    distributive numeral, plural, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Agr. 2.85: duodēna dēscrībit in singulōs hominēs jūgera (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.G. 7.36.7: fossa duplex duodēnum pedum (Lewis & Short)

    Twelve to each person or thing; also twelve with nouns used only in the plural (see pair, on bīnī).

  • sescentī, sescentae, sescenta — dozens, hundreds: a great many

    numeral, plural adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.2.3: quās ego sescentās ūnō tempore accēpī; Ter. Ph. 668: sexcentās proinde scrībitō jam mihi dicās

    Properly six hundred; where English says “dozens” or “hundreds”, Latin says six hundred, very often in prose and verse (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • veniō ad epistulās tuās; quās ego sescentās ūnō tempore accēpī, aliam aliā jūcundiōrem

    I come to your letters: I got dozens of them at once, each more delightful than the lastCic. Att. 7.2.3

  • Duodecim ōva emē, sīs.

    Buy a dozen eggs, will you?composed

See also number, twelfth.
